title: Successive derived quotients form a quotient-linear triangle
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small in the chosen coefficient universe, $B$ a sheaf of commutative rings and $t\in\Gamma(\mathcal C,B)$ a section whose multiplication map $B\xrightarrow{t}B$ is injective. For $j\ge1$ let $R_j=B/t^jB$ be the quotient ring sheaf. Use module sheaves and their unbounded derived categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For $K\in D(B)$ put $K_j=K\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}R_j$ by [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. For every $n>1$ there exists a distinguished triangle in $D(R_n)$
$$\operatorname{Res}_{R_n\to R_{n-1}}K_{n-1}\longrightarrow K_n\longrightarrow\operatorname{Res}_{R_n\to R_1}K_1\longrightarrow(\operatorname{Res}_{R_n\to R_{n-1}}K_{n-1})[1].$$
Restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars] is applied termwise to representing complexes. For any K-flat resolution [def-pc-kflat-complex] with flat terms [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] of a representative of $K$, the first two arrows are induced by multiplication by $t$ and quotient on the second tensor factor, respectively. No boundedness or completeness assumption on $K$ is required.

source.place: Second paragraph: coefficient exact sequence and derived tensor triangle, retaining the R_n-action.

proof.text: Represent $K$ by a complex $G$. Choose a flat-term K-flat resolution $f:P\to G$ using [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]; it exists for an arbitrary unbounded $G$. We will use this same $P$ for all three coefficient sheaves.

Fix $n>1$. Apply [lem-pe-successive-quotient-flat-complex-sequence] to $B,t,n,P$. Its canonical quotient maps make the endpoint tensors $R_n$-complexes, and it gives the degreewise short exact sequence $0\to\operatorname{Res}C_{n-1}\xrightarrow{\alpha}C_n\xrightarrow{\beta}\operatorname{Res}C_1\to0$, where $C_j=R_j\otimes_BP$, with the specified multiplication and quotient formulas.

source.place: Second paragraph, coefficient exact sequence tensored termwise with the flat-term representative.

proof.text: The smallness assumption makes $\operatorname{Mod}(R_n)$ abelian [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle] in this category to step 2. It gives a distinguished triangle $Q_n\operatorname{Res}C_{n-1}\xrightarrow{Q_n\alpha}Q_n C_n\xrightarrow{Q_n\beta}Q_n\operatorname{Res}C_1\xrightarrow{\delta}(Q_n\operatorname{Res}C_{n-1})[1]$ directly in $D(R_n)$.

Apply [lem-pe-restricted-kflat-tensor-identification] with $A=R_n$ and $S=R_{n-1},R_n,R_1$, taking $v$ to be the canonical quotients or the identity. The three objects in step 3 identify with $\operatorname{Res}K_{n-1},K_n,\operatorname{Res}K_1$. Apply its coefficient-map equation to $h=a$ and $h=b$ from step 2: these are $R_n$-linear, though $a$ need not be a ring map. The first two arrows then have formulas $p\otimes\bar c\mapsto p\otimes\overline{tc}$ and $p\otimes\bar c\mapsto p\otimes\bar c$ on the second tensor factor.

source.place: Tag 06YY and the scalar-first/restricted K-flat comparison; tensor exchange from sites-modules.tex Tag 03EK.

proof.text: Write the three isomorphisms of step 4 as $i_-:X_-\to\operatorname{Res}K_{n-1}$, $i_0:X_0\to K_n$, $i_1:X_1\to\operatorname{Res}K_1$. Use first arrow $i_0(Q_n\alpha)i_-^{-1}$, second arrow $i_1(Q_n\beta)i_0^{-1}$ and connecting map $i_-[1]\,\delta\,i_1^{-1}$. This triangle is isomorphic to step 3, hence distinguished by [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The construction applies to every flat-term K-flat resolution, since only these properties of $P$ were used; no bound or completeness was imposed.

source.place: Tag 05RU, derived category distinguished triangles are closed under isomorphism.
